home.overview:
I am an Assistant Professor in the Department of Electronics & Instrumentation Technology at the University of Kashmir. I study antennas and engineered electromagnetic materials, with a focus on shaping radio waves for communication, sensing, and imaging.

My work spans microwave and millimeter-wave antenna systems, metasurfaces, MIMO architectures, and RF circuits. I received my Ph.D. from [IIT Delhi](https://home.iitd.ac.in/) and my M.Tech. from [IIITDM Jabalpur](https://www.iiitdmj.ac.in/).
home.opportunities:
I welcome inquiries from students interested in antennas, electromagnetics, and microwave imaging. Experience with electromagnetic simulation and RF circuit design is useful. Please send a CV and a short description of your research interests by email.

Research admissions and project appointments follow University procedures and formal advertisements. Contact me for the latest availability.

research.title: Lens Antennas
research.description: Thin planar lenses that shape antenna wavefronts to improve gain and support multiple beams. The work explores metasurface and anisotropic designs for low-profile MIMO systems.

research.title: Reconfigurable Metasurfaces
research.description: Planar electromagnetic structures for wave control, including reconfigurable surfaces, absorbers, and polarization conversion for communication and sensing.

research.title: Beamforming and MIMO Antennas
research.description: Compact and high-gain antennas with multiple ports, switched beams, and steerable radiation patterns for microwave and millimetre-wave communication.

research.title: Microwave Imaging and Sensing Systems
research.description: Frequency-diverse antennas and computational imaging methods for dielectric contrast mapping and non-contact sensing.

research.title: RF and Microwave Circuits
research.description: Microwave components that combine filtering, radiation, reconfiguration, and energy harvesting for wireless and sensing applications.

research.title: Metamaterials and Anisotropic Media
research.description: Engineered media for phase correction, enhanced aperture efficiency, and the routing of electromagnetic waves.

gallery.title: Thin planar metasurface lens
gallery.description: A thin resonator-based lens shapes the fields from a three-port antenna array into beams directed along different angles.
gallery.imageAlt: Diagram of a lens above an antenna array, photograph of the fabricated lens, and a 29 GHz radiation pattern
gallery.caption: Lens concept, fabricated prototype, and radiation pattern.

gallery.title: High-gain antenna structures
gallery.description: Anisotropic high–low-epsilon media provide phase correction to improve antenna gain and aperture efficiency.
gallery.imageAlt: Fabricated metamaterial lens structures and an antenna measurement arrangement
gallery.caption: Prototype imagery from the high-gain antenna study.

gallery.title: Multibeam radiation
gallery.description: High-index slabs around an antenna redirect radiation into multiple beams, connecting engineered media with compact antenna design.
gallery.imageAlt: Multibeam antenna configuration, prototype photographs, and radiation patterns
gallery.caption: A glimpse of the multibeam antenna work.

biography.intro: My academic work combines antenna design, electromagnetic materials, and microwave systems. Before joining the University of Kashmir, I held research and teaching appointments at SKUAST-Kashmir, IIT Jammu, and IIT Delhi.
biography.service: I review research for journals in antennas, electromagnetics, and microwave engineering, including IEEE Transactions on Antennas and Propagation, IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters, IEEE Sensors Journal, and IEEE Access.

group.name: RF & Microwave Lab@KU
group.description: Our group investigates antenna systems, metasurfaces, microwave imaging, and RF sensing. We connect the design of electromagnetic structures with practical questions in wireless communication and non-contact measurement.
group.enquiries: Interested in working with us? Email a CV and a short outline of your research interests. We welcome inquiries from prospective Ph.D. scholars and postgraduate students. Appointments and admissions are subject to University rules and formal advertisements.
